name: Utah

context: UT 340: Cover crop is used to reduce sheet, rill, and wind erosion on cropland.
UT 329: No-till applies to all cropland and limits soil disturbance to keep residue on the surface.
UT 603: Herbaceous wind barriers are for cropland where wind erosion is a resource concern.
cover_rules: UT 340: Maximize combined canopy and surface residue cover to a minimum of 90-percent cover during the period of potentially erosive wind or rainfall.
UT 340: Time cover crop establishment with other practices so soil is protected during the critical erosion periods.
residue: UT 329: Maintain a minimum of 60 percent residue cover on the soil surface throughout the year.
UT 329: Do not shred residue after harvest; shredding makes it more susceptible to movement by wind or water.
UT 329: Stubble height for snow trapping is at least 10 inches for rows under 15 inches and at least 15 inches for wider rows.
barriers: UT 603: Barriers need a minimum expected height of 1.5 feet and porosity of 40 to 50 percent, set perpendicular to the prevailing wind.
UT 603: Barrier spacing must not exceed 10 times the planned herbaceous barrier height.
UT 589: Trap strips are at least 15 feet wide if 1 foot or taller, and at least 25 feet wide if under 1 foot.
windbreak: UT 380: The protected zone is 10H on the leeward side and 2H on the windward side; set the windbreak perpendicular to the wind.
UT 380: Select species for planting that are taller than the height of the crop.
grazing: UT 528: Plan grazing to keep adequate ground cover from plant canopy, litter, and trampled residue to protect the soil from wind and water.
UT 528: Minimize grazing animal impact on areas that have high soil erosion potential.
drought: UT 528: Develop and document contingencies to prepare for episodic disturbances such as drought.
seeding: UT 550: Calculate seeding rates on a pure live seed (PLS) basis.
UT 550: A native seeding must be a minimum of 55% native species, by percent of the mix, not lbs/ac.
crp: UT CRP: No grazing activity during the Primary Nesting Season (April 1 – July 15) where that option applies.
disturbed: UT 484: Mulch with straw or grass hay at a rate that gives a minimum 70 percent ground cover.
UT 484: Wood mulch needs a minimum 2-inch thickness so it stays in place in strong wind.
dunes: UT 342: Sand dune plants must survive being buried by blowing sand; include sand fences or brush matting.
UT TN24: Mammoth wildrye is long lived on well-drained inland sand dunes; recommended seeding rate is 15 lb/ac.

cover.name: Winter wheat
cover.note: UT 340: Cool-season. Broadcast 60-160 lbs/acre; disk lightly or cultipack to cover.

cover.name: Rye
cover.note: UT 340: Cool-season. Broadcast 90-160 lbs/acre; disk lightly or cultipack to cover.

cover.name: Barley
cover.note: UT 340: Cool-season. Broadcast 80-125 lbs/acre; harrow or light disk to cover.

cover.name: Hairy vetch
cover.note: UT 340: Cool-season legume. Broadcast 25-40 lbs/ac, follow with light disk.

cover.name: Buckwheat
cover.note: UT 340: Quick canopy closure. Broadcast up to 96 lb/acre; incorporate with harrow or disk.

cover.name: Sorghum-sudan
cover.note: UT 340: Warm-season. Use higher rate for weed control.

coverPlant.text: UT 340: Warm-season covers are generally suited to be planted in late spring/early summer and terminated before frost.
UT 340: Cool-season covers can be planted in late fall or early spring for a spring termination.

seedWin.text: UT TN24: Dormant fall planting is recommended for Russian wildrye because of seed dormancy.

shrubs.name: Fourwing saltbush
advice: UT TN24: Fourwing saltbush is well suited to deep, well-drained sandy soil and sand dunes.

shrubs.name: Big sagebrush
advice: UT TN24: Big sagebrush grows on arid plains, valleys, and foothills in the 8-18 inch annual rainfall areas.
